# Code review: `200cd0a0…HEAD`

Scope: explicit range, merge-base `2f860c4` → `e176de0`. 34 files, +1,779 −202. Nothing was modified, installed, run or posted.
Profile: safe-client-gateway · TypeScript/NestJS on Fastify · vitest · biome and tsc · rules taken from AGENTS.md (10 non-negotiables) and 14 guides in `docs/agents/` · all 9 areas had something to review.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | **Approve**, score 93/100 |
| **What held the score down** | One Medium coupling finding in architecture, and three Low findings in conventions and KISS |
| **Fix first** | The Core 402 error message (KIS-001). It's user-facing and a one-line fix. |
| **Blocking** | Nothing is P0, P1 or P2. Everything is P3. |

The gating logic itself is sound. Every request passes the auth guard, then the membership check, then the `copilot_scans` entitlement, then the check that the Safe belongs to the Space. A missing catalog row now denies instead of allowing. Old-shape cache entries are treated as misses, and a rolling deploy works in both directions. The test coverage checks each of those gates and the order they run in.

## Scores by area

| Area | Score | From |
|---|---|---|
| Architecture | 92 | 1 Medium, confirmed |
| Conventions | 94 | 2 Low, confirmed (1 more disputed and set aside) |
| KISS | 97 | 1 Low, confirmed |
| DRY | 100 | 1 Nit, disputed. Nits don't cost points. |
| Security, Bugs, Regression, Testing, Performance | 100 | no findings |

## Findings (all P3, worth a ticket or a quick fix)

**ARC-001 · Medium · confirmed: the Spaces controller imports safe-shield's internal DTOs and validation schema**
`src/modules/spaces/routes/safe-shield/space-safe-shield.controller.ts:28-31`, and the same pattern in `space-safe-shield.service.ts:9-13`
- The new controller imports `CounterpartyAnalysisRequestSchema` and the Swagger DTOs (`CounterpartyAnalysisDto`, `CounterpartyAnalysisRequestDto`, `SingleRecipientAnalysisDto`) from `@/modules/safe-shield/entities/...`.
- That breaks AGENTS.md rule 4 and `module-structure.md:75`, which say a module is imported only through its `domain/`. It also goes against the diff's own `ISafeShieldAnalysis` comment, which says consumers shouldn't reach into safe-shield's HTTP layer.
- **Risk:** if someone changes one of these DTOs or schemas for safe-shield's own endpoint, the Spaces API's validation and Swagger change too, and nobody touches the Spaces module.
- **Fix:** give the Spaces routes their own DTOs and schema under `spaces/routes/safe-shield/entities/`. Alternatively, move the shared contract into `safe-shield/domain/`.

**KIS-001 · Low · confirmed: the Core 402 message says counterparty analysis is gated, but it isn't**
`src/modules/safe-shield/errors/copilot-core-disabled.error.ts:13`, with the same wording at `:6` and `src/modules/safe-shield/guards/copilot-core-gating.guard.ts:6`
- The message reads `'Recipient and counterparty analysis require a paid Space on Copilot.'`.
- The guard is only on `analyzeRecipient`. Counterparty analysis stays free on Core, as `.env.sample.json` and `configuration.ts:495` both say, and the tests assert.
- Clients reading the 402 body will be told the wrong thing.
- **Fix:** say "Recipient analysis requires…" in all three places.

**CNV-001 · Low · confirmed: the new flag comment names no owner**
`src/config/entities/configuration.ts:495`
- The comment is `// Disables Core's recipient-check. Remove once no client calls it.` It gives a removal condition but no owner.
- `configuration-and-flags.md:51,57` requires owner plus condition, in the same shape as `mfaStepUp` six lines above.
- **Fix:** add `Owner: <team/ticket>`, for example the PLA-1964 ticket from the branch name.

**CNV-002 · Low · confirmed: new safe-shield files are in new root-level `errors/` and `guards/` folders**
`src/modules/safe-shield/errors/copilot-core-disabled.error.ts:1`, and the same for `errors/copilot-core-disabled.exception-filter.ts:1` and `guards/copilot-core-gating.guard.ts:1`
- `module-structure.md:8` says the standard layout is mandatory for new files. `api-dtos-and-validation.md` puts errors in `domain/errors/` and filters in `domain/exception-filters/`. `nestjs-patterns.md:51` puts guards in `routes/guards/`.
- This same diff creates `safe-shield/domain/` and puts the matching entitlements files in the right places.
- **Fix:** move the error and filter to `safe-shield/domain/errors/` and `safe-shield/domain/exception-filters/`. Move the guard to `safe-shield/routes/guards/`.

**DRY-001 · Nit · disputed: the transaction shape is typed inline instead of reusing a named type**
`src/modules/safe-shield/domain/safe-shield-analysis.interface.ts:28` and `src/modules/spaces/routes/safe-shield/space-safe-shield.service.ts:52`
- The validator's view: `{ to; value; data; operation }` duplicates what `TransactionBaseSchema` already defines.
- The refuter's view: the interface has to mirror the existing `SafeShieldService.analyzeCounterparty` signature, which the compiler enforces, and `z.infer` of that schema gives `string`, not `Hex`.
- What's left is minor: the service could reference the interface's parameter type instead of restating it.

## Not sure about these (confidence under 40, not scored)
- **CNV-003** at `space-safe-shield.service.ts:13`: the service imports `Space` from `.entity.db` while its controller (`:32`) imports it from `domain/`. Existing services in `spaces` are already split about evenly between the two, so this follows existing practice rather than breaking it.
- **DRY-002** at `src/__tests__/util/space-fixtures.ts:16`: three older local `createSpaceForSigner` copies were left in place. This was refuted: those copies return the space UUID as `spaceId`, while the shared helper returns the numeric id, and all three files are outside the diff.

## Ruled out
- Checking the entitlement before checking that the Safe is in the Space: bugs flagged it and security cleared it. Non-members are rejected first, so a Space's plan state is never shown to an outsider.
- `countBySpaceId` → `countSeatsBySpaceId` in `billing.service.ts`: this came in with a merge from main and brings a caller up to date with a method that was already renamed.
- The shape change to the cached `FeatureGrant`: an entry the new version can't read is treated as a cache miss, and the older schema accepts the new field. The extra cost is limited to the cache lifetime during a deploy.
- The new catalog-gap denial: for keys that already exist it behaves the same, because `staticGrant(0)` already blocked.
- Two items passed between areas and dropped: whether `FeatureGrant.enabled` duplicates `quota: 0` (KISS gave it to DRY), and whether the one-filter-per-error pattern should be shared (DRY gave it to conventions). In both cases the pass that raised it said it found no actual defect.

## What this review didn't cover
- No tests, lint or tsc were run, as you asked, so none of the claims above rest on running code.
- The "worth tidying" cleanup proposals and the fix/ticket/skip step were skipped because this was a read-only run. No "since your last run" comparison file was written.

## How this was produced
Nine category passes ran in parallel and returned 7 findings. Every finding was then checked by one agent trying to prove it and a second trying to disprove it.
- Adjudicated **7 of 7**: 4 confirmed, 3 disputed (2 of those fell below the confidence cutoff). None were refuted outright. No handed-off items needed to be turned into findings, and nothing was deduplicated.
- The overall score is the weighted average of the nine area scores, which comes to 93. No rule that caps the score applied.
